title: Stereotaxic Injection by Iontophoresis
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: Preparation and Take Down for Surgical Procedures
Sterilized Surgical Tool Set in Autoclave Tray
Scalpel handle (Fine Science Tools 10003-12 or equivalent)
Iris forceps (Fine Science Tools 11064-07 or equivalent)

Materials (Please note this section is a catch-all for all procedures, not all supplies and equipment are used for every surgical procedure. Refer to SOPs for complete list of required supplies for each specific procedure.)
Nair Hair Removal Cream (Amazon B00R4HWYNI or equivalent)
Black Tempura Paint (Sargent Art 22-7185 or equivalent)
Sugi pointed sterile swabs (Kettenbach 3061 or equivalent)
Sterile Drill Bits, 0.5/0.4 (NeoBurr FG1/4 or equivalent)
Sterile Drill Bits, 1.4/1.1 (NeoBurr FG4 or equivalent)
Sterile Drill Bits 1.0/4.2 (NeoBurr EF4 or equivalent)
Non-Sterile Gloves (Microflex Ultraform Gloves or equivalent)
Kwik Cast (World Precision Instruments Kwik-Cast or equivalent)

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Environment
steps.instruction: Clean and organize the surgical area to maintain sterility.

substeps.instruction: Remove hand jewelry, wash hands with soap and water, don exam gloves, and spray gloves with alcohol.
Turn on microscope lights, bead sterilizer, and heating pad (set to 37.0 ± 0.5°C).
Spray surgery area with disinfectant spray cleaner, wait 5 minutes, and wipe with a kimwipe.
Wipe down the surgical rig, heating pad, nose cone, bite bar, light casings, stereotaxic knobs, and microscope surfaces with alcohol.
Wipe down the drill and drill stand with alcohol.
Clean the isoflurane induction chamber with disinfectant spray.
Place a sterile drape on the disinfected area, white side up and blue side down.
Drop sterile cotton swabs, kimwipes, and gauze onto the drape without touching them.
Place sterilized surgery tools on the drape, avoiding the instrument tips.
If required, spray a well from the designated jar with 70% Ethanol and place on the drape.
Cover the surgical rig heating pad with Press ‘n’ Seal.

steps.title: Prepare ACSF Irrigation System
steps.instruction: Set up the sterile Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid (ACSF) delivery system.

substeps.instruction: Fill a 10 or 20 ml syringe with sterile ACSF.
Attach a 25G 5/8” needle to a sterile 0.2 μm syringe filter, then attach the ACSF syringe to the filter.
Ensure fluid is only expelled from the syringe through the filter (do not pull fluid back through the needle).
Place the assembly on the sterile drape.

steps.title: Prepare General Surgical Supplies
steps.instruction: Prepare the multi-well plate with necessary reagents for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Fill one well with 1 ml Nair.
Fill one well with 1 ml Betadine solution and soak three swabs.
If required, fill three wells with black cement powder (4:1 cement to paint ratio).
If performing HP+C, use sterile forceps to place pieces of sterile Gelfoam in one well.
Place a coverslip in a well and cover with 70% Ethanol to soak using forceps.
Fill the Gelfoam well with ACSF to soak.
Fill one or two additional wells with ACSF.
Disinfect the drill with 70% Ethanol and attach the drill bit.

steps.title: Prepare Iontophoretic Injection Pipette
steps.instruction: Prepare the glass pipette and virus for iontophoretic injection.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a 1.2 mm diameter pulled glass pipette with the tip already broken.
Remove virus aliquot from -80ºC freezer, thaw at room temperature, spin down in mini centrifuge, and store on wet ice.
Fill one well of a 24-well plate with Betadine and a second with Nair; place on the sterile drape.
Fill the pipette with virus immediately before injection to prevent clogging.

steps.title: Prepare Nanoject Injection System
steps.instruction: Set up and load the Nanoject automatic injector.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a Nanoject-specific pulled and broken pipette.
Remove virus aliquot from -80ºC freezer, thaw at room temperature, spin down in mini centrifuge, and store on wet ice.
Fill one well of a 24-well plate with Betadine and a second with Nair; place on the sterile drape.
Backfill the pipette using a 30g, 2” Hamilton syringe filled with mineral oil by depressing the plunger slowly to the shoulder, ensuring no bubbles are introduced.
Set the injector wire plunger to the 'home position' (tip flush or slightly recessed from the end of the collet).
Insert the blunt end of the pipette through the collet and large O-ring, pushing it onto the wire plunger until it seats in the white spacer, then tighten the collet.
Press and hold the 'EMPTY' button to expel 4-5 drops of oil and remove air bubbles (do not extend plunger to full length).
Spin down virus for 10-15 seconds; use a P20 micropipette with a microfil tip to draw ~2 µl of virus and aspirate it onto Parafilm.
Lower the pipette tip into the virus sample using the stereotaxic apparatus.
Press and hold the 'FILL' button to draw up the desired amount of virus without introducing air bubbles.
Set volume switches 1-5 to D-D-U-D-D for a standard injection of 50.6 nl per press at a rate of 23 nl/sec.

steps.title: Set Up Anesthesia System
steps.instruction: Configure the gas delivery system for animal induction and maintenance.

substeps.instruction: Set vacuum gauge to 10-15 PSI and verify all vacuum lines for the induction chamber and nosecone scoop.
Connect the induction chamber to Isoflurane and Oxygen.
Turn on the oxygen concentrator and set the Oxygen regulator to 0.8-1.0 L/min.
Open vacuum and Isoflurane valves, directing flow to the induction chamber.

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse using the induction chamber.

substeps.instruction: Obtain preoperative weight and record cage number, sex, and birthdate.
Place the mouse in the induction chamber and set the Isoflurane regulator to 5.0 (5%), noting the start time.
Once the mouse is unconscious (approx. one breath every 3 seconds, no movement), turn off the Isoflurane while keeping oxygen and vacuum lines open.
Transfer the mouse to the surgical rig.

steps.title: Secure Animal on Surgical Rig
steps.instruction: Position and stabilize the mouse for surgery.

substeps.instruction: Secure the mouse in ear bars or the specified clamping mechanism, ensuring the head is straight, symmetrical, and immobile.
Secure the nose cone over the snout and ensure the body is resting comfortably on the heating pad.
Redirect gas flow from the induction chamber to the surgical rig and set Isoflurane to ~1.5-2%.
Turn off the induction chamber vacuum line and close the lid.
Monitor breathing and response to toe pinch, adjusting Isoflurane levels as necessary.

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Clear and disinfect the head area for incision.

substeps.instruction: Apply Puralube to a cotton swab to push whiskers away from the field and apply a generous amount of Puralube to the eyes.
Use non-sterile scissors to shorten hair from the top of the head and left side of the face (behind ears and between eyes). Wipe scissors with alcohol after use.
Apply Nair with a non-sterile cotton swab to remove remaining hair; remove Nair within 25 seconds.
Remove all Nair using clean non-sterile cotton swabs or alcohol wipes (one swipe per swab).
Wipe the head surface with ACSF or alcohol wipes and clean with kimwipes to prevent Nair burns.
Disinfect the head with 3 rounds of alternating Betadine-soaked sterile swabs and alcohol wipes; do not wipe off the final Betadine application.
Discard the hair-catch gauze from under the mouse into a biohazard bin.
Cover the mouse's body up to the surgical site with saran wrap.

steps.title: Post-Operative Take-down
steps.instruction: Clean the surgical area and sterilize tools after the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Change gloves after the animal is removed from the rig and post-operative care is complete.
Disinfect the surgery area as per the initial setup steps.
Dispose of syringes, blades, drill bits, and needles in the biohazard sharps container.
Spray tools with pH neutral surgical tool cleaner, wipe with kimwipe or alcohol swab to remove residue, wrap in autoclave pack, and label with initials and date.
If tools are needed again the same day, use the hot bead dry sterilizer.
Disinfect ear bars with 70% Ethanol and return to the rig.
Release air from drill lines by pressing pedals until pressure reads 0 psi and turn off the wall valve.
Turn off vacuum and oxygen sources via stopcocks.

description: General principles for “tips only” aseptic surgery
